home-remodeling.local_heading: Two ways to own in Bal Harbour
intro_paragraphs: Bal Harbour is barely ten blocks of barrier island, and it holds two very different kinds of home. West of Collins Avenue, behind a staffed gate, the estate section ranges from mid-century modern houses to Mediterranean Revival and new construction on Bal Bay Drive, Harbour Way, and the bayfront. East of Collins, the towers climb from the Plaza of Bal Harbour, built in 1965, to Oceana, finished in 2016. High-end remodeling here means either taking a mid-century house down to block and beam or gutting a tower residence to the slab, and we do both.

Permits go through the Bal Harbour Village Building Department at Village Hall on 96th Street, and the Village reads plans closely. Anything that changes the exterior, from windows and doors to paint and additions, needs a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Architectural Review Board before the building permit moves. Interior-only work goes straight to plan review. Then add the practical layer: this is a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so openings need Miami-Dade product approvals, and much of the village sits in AE flood zones, where FEMA substantial-improvement rules can shape how far a renovation of an older home can go.

PGX Builders Group brings over two decades of South Florida building and more than 150 completed remodels and additions to every job, each one permitted and inspected. In Bal Harbour that experience shows up as a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site every working day, and crews who treat a guard gate and a service elevator with equal respect. One licensed team, Lic. CGC1539072, carries the project from estimate to warranty. No handoffs, no shrugs.

faqs.q: Do I need Architectural Review Board approval to remodel in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: Only if the work touches the exterior. Windows, doors, paint colors, driveways, fences, and additions all go before the Village's Architectural Review Board for a Certificate of Appropriateness before the building permit is issued. A remodel that stays entirely inside, even a full gut, is submitted directly to the Building Department for plan review. We map this out at the estimate stage so board timing never surprises anyone.

faqs.q: How long does permitting take in Bal Harbour Village?
faqs.a: Longer than homeowners hope, shorter than the horror stories. Bal Harbour runs its own Building Department out of Village Hall, applications are filed in person, and review is genuinely thorough. Interior-only scopes tend to move faster, while anything touching the exterior must clear the Architectural Review Board calendar first. We prepare complete submittals so comments come back once, and we build realistic permit time into the schedule instead of pretending it away.

faqs.q: Can you handle a full remodel inside an older tower like the Balmoral or the Plaza?
faqs.a: Yes, and the older Collins Avenue towers are where experience earns its keep. Buildings from the 1960s through the 1980s are deep in Florida's milestone-inspection era, so associations review renovation plans carefully and most require licensed, insured contractors with formal approval before demolition. We assemble the association package, book service elevators, respect quiet hours, and protect common areas, so the only thing your neighbors notice is the finished result.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a whole-home remodel in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: There is no honest per-square-foot figure that covers both a bayfront estate and a tower flow-through, so we won't pretend otherwise. Scope drives cost: structural changes, window packages, cabinetry level, and stone selection matter far more than raw square footage. What we commit to is a fixed, written scope with real allowances before construction begins, priced as the high-end contractor we are rather than the lowest bid you will receive.

faqs.q: Will FEMA's substantial-improvement rule limit my renovation?
faqs.a: It can, and it is better to know before you fall in love with a floor plan. In AE flood zones, when improvement costs cross a defined share of the structure's value, the building may have to be brought into compliance with current flood-elevation rules. For some of Bal Harbour's original houses, that math changes strategy: phase the work, or commit to the larger project deliberately. We run those numbers with the Village early, before design money is spent.

kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchens for Bal Harbour estates and oceanfront condos. Cabinetry, stone, and layout changes, fully permitted. Call PGX Builders at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen that earns the view
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Kitchen remodeling for Bal Harbour houses and tower residences: custom cabinetry, stone counters, islands, and full layout changes, designed around how you cook and delivered permitted, inspected, and supervised by a licensed builder.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Kitchens on a very small island
intro_paragraphs: Bal Harbour kitchens tend to predate the way their owners entertain now. In the estate section, houses along Camden Drive still carry galley kitchens walled off from the living space, while residences in older towers like the Kenilworth and the Tiffany of Bal Harbour often hold original builder layouts from their first decades. Owners here don't want a refresh; they want custom cabinetry, a real island, stone chosen at the slab yard, and a kitchen finally open to the water view they paid for.

A kitchen that stays within its footprint is usually an interior-only permit, filed directly with the Bal Harbour Village Building Department. Knock down the wall to the dining room and you're into structural review; move the kitchen across a condo unit and you're routing drains and vents through a concrete building, which takes engineering and association sign-off, not optimism. Older towers along Collins Avenue also sit in Florida's milestone-inspection era, so associations read renovation plans more carefully than they did a decade ago. We prepare packages that pass both reviews the first time.

A PGX kitchen job runs like a well-plated service: everything is decided before the heat comes on. Cabinetry shop drawings are approved before demolition, stone is at the fabricator while rough trades run, and appliance specs are locked so the electrician never guesses. Our site lead walks the job every day, floors and elevators get protected like they belong to someone we want to work for again, because they do, and the schedule you sign at contract is the schedule we actually manage to.

faqs.q: Can I move my kitchen to a different part of my condo?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and the honest answer starts with a feasibility check, not a promise. Drains need slope and a path to the building's plumbing risers, which means the slab, the unit below, and the association's alteration rules all get a vote. In some Bal Harbour towers the move is straightforward; in others it is limited to a few feet. We investigate first, then design what the building can actually support.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel in Bal Harbour need Architectural Review Board approval?
faqs.a: Usually not. The board reviews exterior changes, and a kitchen that stays inside the walls goes directly to the Building Department for permits and inspections. The exception is when the project adds or changes a window or door, which does trigger board review. In a condominium the second gate is the association, which has its own approval process. We tell you which reviews apply before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: Plan in months, not weeks, and let cabinetry set the tempo. Custom cabinetry carries real lead times, so we order it early and run permitting, demolition, and rough trades while it is in fabrication. A straightforward kitchen might run a few months from contract to cooking; one with structural changes or association logistics runs longer. The schedule we give you reflects Bal Harbour's actual pace, not a brochure's.

faqs.q: What does a custom kitchen cost in this area?
faqs.a: Wide range, honestly earned. Cabinetry grade, stone selection, appliance package, and whether walls move matter far more than square footage. A high-end Bal Harbour kitchen is a six-figure conversation more often than not, and we would rather tell you that at the first meeting than surprise you at the last. Every number we commit to arrives in writing, with allowances spelled out.

faqs.q: Who handles my building's renovation requirements?
faqs.a: We do, and we prefer it that way. Bal Harbour associations typically want licensed and insured contractors, certificates of insurance naming the association, approved plans, elevator reservations, and strict work hours; some collect deposits against damage to common areas. We have managed those requirements in occupied luxury buildings for years, and we build their calendar into yours, so approval delays don't get billed as surprises.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling for Bal Harbour Homes & Condos, FL
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Primary suites, frameless showers, and waterproofing done right in Bal Harbour homes and condo towers. Licensed Miami GC. Call (786) 273-2524 today.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers, and freestanding tubs for Bal Harbour residences — waterproofed to a standard the ocean respects, permitted through the Village Building Department, and checked by a supervisor every single day.
intro_paragraphs: In a village pressed between the Atlantic and Biscayne Bay, bathrooms age fast and fail expensively. Estate-section houses on Park Drive and Bal Cross Drive still hide original tubs and four-inch tile from their first owners; residences at the Majestic Tower or the Plaza of Bal Harbour often carry builder-grade bathrooms several fashions out of date. The remodel owners actually want is a true primary suite: curbless shower behind frameless glass, freestanding tub, stone on every surface, and ventilation that can cope with humidity eleven months a year.

Bathroom work in Bal Harbour is permitted through the Village Building Department, and because most of it is interior, it skips the Architectural Review Board and goes straight into plan review. In a high-rise, the stakes are different: your shower pan sits on top of someone's ceiling, so associations require approved contractors, insurance certificates, and proof the waterproofing is being inspected, not assumed. In towers old enough for Florida's milestone inspections, plumbing risers and shut-offs get attention too. We schedule tie-ins with building engineers so your neighbors keep their water and their patience.

We build bathrooms in the order that prevents callbacks: substrate flat, slopes correct, waterproofing membrane flood-tested before a single tile goes down. It is the least glamorous week of the project and the one that decides whether the marble lasts. Stone is templated and set by installers we trust with veined slabs, fixtures go in against the written scope, and a PGX supervisor signs off daily. Twenty-plus years in South Florida taught us where bathrooms fail, and we spend our attention exactly there.

faqs.q: Does a bathroom remodel in Bal Harbour require a permit?
faqs.a: Yes. Moving plumbing, replacing electrical, rebuilding shower pans, and changing fixtures all require permits and inspections through the Bal Harbour Village Building Department, even when the footprint never changes. That is good news, not red tape: inspected waterproofing is what stands between your marble and a slow leak. Unpermitted bathroom work also has a way of surfacing during a sale, at the least convenient possible moment.

faqs.q: What will my condo association require before work starts?
faqs.a: Expect a formal alteration agreement, proof of licensing and insurance, drawings for anything touching plumbing or walls, elevator scheduling, and defined work hours. Wet areas get particular scrutiny because a failed pan affects the unit below, and in Bal Harbour's older towers the era of milestone inspections has made boards more careful, not less. We assemble the full package and walk it through management before we schedule demolition.

faqs.q: Can you replace the old plumbing, not just the finishes?
faqs.a: Yes, and in many cases you should. Houses from Bal Harbour's first decades often still run galvanized or first-generation copper lines, and tower bathrooms tie into risers that deserve inspection while walls are open. A remodel is the cheapest moment you will ever have to replace supply lines, valves, and drains. We scope it up front so the decision is yours, made once, while access is free.

faqs.q: How long does a bathroom renovation take here?
faqs.a: A full primary bath typically runs a couple of months of construction once permits are in hand, and waterproofing is one reason why. Membranes cure and get flood-tested before tile, and we do not compress that step for anyone's calendar. Condo projects add association approvals and elevator logistics at the front end. We publish the sequence in the contract schedule, so you always know which week you are in.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a high-end bathroom in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: Less than a kitchen, more than a refresh, and mostly driven by stone, glass, and fixtures. A primary suite with slab surfaces, a curbless shower, and quality plumbing hardware is a serious investment, and pretending otherwise helps no one. We price from a fixed scope with named materials, so comparing our number against others means comparing the same bathroom, which, in our experience, it rarely is at first.

home-additions.meta_description: Rear extensions, second stories, and in-law suites in Bal Harbour's gated estate section. Engineered, ARB approved, fully permitted. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: More room on a finished island
home-additions.hero_sub: Home additions for the estate section of Bal Harbour: rear extensions, second stories, and garage conversions with engineered foundations, tie-beam upgrades, Architectural Review Board approvals, and daily supervision from a licensed GC.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house behind the gate
intro_paragraphs: Nobody is making more land in Bal Harbour. The village was master-planned in the 1930s and essentially built out decades ago, which means owners on Bal Cross Drive or Bal Bay Drive who love their street but not their square footage have one real option: build onto the house they have. Rear extensions toward the garden, second stories that capture bay views, and garage conversions into guest or staff quarters are the projects we see most, often as part of a larger renovation.

An addition is exactly the kind of project the Village of Bal Harbour reviews hardest. New construction and additions require Architectural Review Board approval and a Certificate of Appropriateness before the Building Department issues a permit, and the design has to respect setbacks, lot coverage, and the character of a very tidy village. Then come the technical layers: High-Velocity Hurricane Zone engineering, foundations and tie-beams designed for coastal wind loads, and, in AE flood zones, FEMA substantial-improvement math that can determine whether an ambitious addition triggers elevation requirements for the whole house.

Additions are where a general contractor either coordinates or improvises, and improvisation shows. PGX runs additions with the structure decided on paper: engineered drawings, a fixed written scope, and a schedule that sequences foundation, shell, tie-in, and finishes so the existing house stays livable and dry. Deliveries are timed for narrow gated streets, a supervisor walks the site each day, and the crew that ties the new roof into the old one is the same crew accountable for the warranty. That is what one team from estimate to closeout actually means.

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to my Bal Harbour home?
faqs.a: Often yes, but the answer lives in the structure, not the wish. Many original estate-section houses were built with foundations and tie-beams sized for one story, so a second floor starts with a structural evaluation and honest engineering. Some houses carry the load with targeted upgrades; others want new columns and footings. The design also goes before the Architectural Review Board, so massing and style matter as much as math.

faqs.q: Does the Architectural Review Board review additions?
faqs.a: Yes, additions and new construction are exactly what the board exists to review. Your project needs a Certificate of Appropriateness before the Building Department issues its permit, which means drawings that show the addition respecting the streetscape, the setbacks, and the house it joins. We prepare board-ready presentations and attend the meetings, because an addition approved on the first pass is worth months of calendar.

faqs.q: Will FEMA rules affect my addition?
faqs.a: They can. Much of Bal Harbour sits in AE flood zones, and when the cost of improvements crosses a defined share of the existing structure's value, flood-elevation compliance can come into play for the whole building. That threshold shapes smart addition design: sometimes the answer is a leaner scope, sometimes it is embracing a larger project done to current standards. We put that analysis on the table before design fees, not after.

faqs.q: I live in a condo on Collins Avenue. Can I add space?
faqs.a: Not in the way a house can, and we will say so plainly. Terraces and exterior walls are common elements, so enclosing or extending them requires association consent and Village approval, and neither is guaranteed. The realistic path to more space in a tower is combining adjacent units, which is a substantial construction project we do take on: structural review, systems integration, association approvals, and one seamless residence at the end.

faqs.q: How long does a home addition take from idea to done?
faqs.a: Measured honestly: months of design, engineering, board review, and permitting before ground breaks, then months of construction after. The variables are the board calendar, the permit review cycle, and how much structure the addition touches. What we control, we commit to in writing: a sequenced schedule, a supervisor on site, and a house kept livable and weathertight while it grows. What we don't control, we tell you about early.

outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, and impact openings for Bal Harbour, FL homes. ARB approvals and permits handled by a licensed GC. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms between the bay and the beach
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Outdoor living and exterior work for Bal Harbour homes — terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, and impact openings, taken through Architectural Review Board approval and Village permits by one licensed, insured team.
outdoor-living.local_heading: The outdoor life, village rules included
intro_paragraphs: Bal Harbour weather makes the case for outdoor rooms; Bal Harbour real estate makes the case for doing them properly. In the gated estate section, houses on Harbour Way and along the bayfront pair mid-century architecture with terraces, pools, and dockside lawns that deserve better than a paver refresh. Owners here commission covered outdoor living with tongue-and-groove ceilings, summer kitchens built around real appliances, pergolas engineered rather than assembled, and driveways and facades that finally match the interior renovation money already spent.

Exterior work is precisely where Bal Harbour Village looks closest. Driveways, fences, paint colors, awnings, windows, and doors all require Architectural Review Board approval and a Certificate of Appropriateness before the Building Department will issue the permit — yes, including the paint. Structures like pergolas and summer kitchens need engineering for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads, impact openings need Miami-Dade product approvals, and work near the seawall on bayfront lots can bring county environmental review into the picture. We sequence the approvals so the project starts once and finishes once.

Outdoor work on a barrier island is a materials exam: salt air grades every hinge, fastener, and light fixture, and it grades hard. PGX specifies marine-grade hardware, stainless fasteners, and finishes chosen for the coast, then builds them under the same discipline as our interiors — fixed scope in writing, daily supervision, protection for the landscaping and the neighbors' patience. When a re-roof or facade repaint joins the project, we coordinate the trades under one contract, so accountability never gets subcontracted away.

faqs.q: Do I need approval just to repaint my house in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: Yes. Exterior paint is on the Architectural Review Board's list, along with driveways, fences, awnings, windows, and doors, and the board issues a Certificate of Appropriateness before the permit side proceeds. It is the price of living in a village that stays this composed. We treat the submittal as part of the job: color schedules, samples, and drawings prepared so approval is a meeting, not a season.

faqs.q: Can I build a summer kitchen by the pool?
faqs.a: At a house, yes: gas, electrical, and plumbing all get permitted, the structure gets engineered for wind, and the finished kitchen is something you can insure and resell with a straight face. On a condo terrace, the association owns that conversation, and open flame is usually a short one. We confirm what your property allows before design starts, so nobody falls for a rendering that can't be built.

faqs.q: What outdoor materials actually survive salt air?
faqs.a: Marine-grade stainless steel, powder-coated aluminum, dense hardwoods, porcelain pavers, and stone with the right sealer all hold up here. Standard hardware, mild steel, and bargain fixtures announce themselves within a year or two, usually as rust streaks down something expensive. We specify coastal-rated materials in the written scope by name, because on a barrier island the cheap version is always the more expensive one.

faqs.q: Can you build near the seawall on a bayfront lot?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right sequence. Terraces, decks, and landscape structures near the water involve setbacks, and work at or over the seawall itself can bring Miami-Dade County environmental review into the project alongside Village approvals. None of that is a reason not to build; it is a reason to design with the rules in view from day one. We flag the regulatory pieces during the walk-through, not after mobilization.

faqs.q: What does outdoor living construction cost in Bal Harbour?
faqs.a: It scales with ambition. A pergola and paver terrace is one budget; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, lighting, and a new driveway is another entirely. Coastal-rated materials and engineered structures cost more than their inland cousins and are worth every dollar the first hurricane season. We prefer to scope your actual project rather than quote a fantasy average, and the scope arrives priced, in writing.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Show us the terrace, the pool deck, or the facade. We'll bring a scope that survives both the board and the weather, in English o en español.
